This is done by minimizing the $L_2$ norm between the target camera pose and the source camera poses [S1]:

The claim states that the process involves minimizing the L2 norm between the target camera pose and the source camera poses. Source [S1], specifically in Section 3.1 'Source Image Selection', provides the mathematical formula: `source imgs = top V ||Pt - Pi||_2`. Here, `Pt` represents the target camera's external matrix (pose) and `Pi` represents the source camera's external matrix (pose). The term `||Pt - Pi||_2` explicitly denotes the L2 norm (Euclidean distance) between these poses. The method selects the top V images with the minimum values of this norm, which is equivalent to minimizing the L2 norm to find the most similar source images.
